findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are not filtered out when the search query is empty
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early on line 62 when `!searchQuery.trim()`, before applying the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` filter on line 67. As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still displayed by default when the search bar is empty and are only hidden after the user types a search query.

findings.title: BrowserReportSerializer age/timestamp validation fails on 0 values and when both fields are omitted
findings.body:
`BrowserReportSerializer` has two validation bugs for `age` and `timestamp`:
1. `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`, which evaluate to `False` when `age` or `timestamp` is `0` (a common valid value for `age` when a browser report is delivered immediately). A report containing `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1640995200000}` will bypass `validate_timestamp`'s mutual-exclusivity check.
2. Both `age` and `timestamp` are declared with `required=False` and no object-level `validate()` check ensures that at least one of them is provided, so reports missing both fields are accepted as valid.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results positionally via events.values()
findings.body: In `fetch_error_details`, `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dictionary mapping `node_id` to event data whose iteration order is not guaranteed to match `node_ids` (for example, `DjangoNodeStorage.get_multi` builds the dict from an unordered `WHERE id IN (...)` query and omits missing keys, and caching layers return cache hits before backend fetches). Iterating with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can pair an `event_id` with another event's payload or misalign entries when a node is missing. Look up each event by its generated `node_id` in `events` instead.

findings.title: renderDefaultHeadCell passes display label column.name instead of column.key to fieldAlignment
findings.body: `renderDefaultHeadCell` computes header alignment via `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType)`. When custom `columns` are provided, `column.name` is the display label (e.g. `'Count of Span Duration'`) while `column.key` is the actual query field/function (e.g. `'count(span.duration)'`), and `column.type` is optional on `TabularColumn` (and not populated from `tableData.meta.fields[column.key]` when `columns` is passed). Passing `column.name` instead of `column.key` prevents `fieldAlignment` from recognizing aggregate/numeric fields when `column.type` is omitted, causing numeric headers to be left-aligned instead of right-aligned.
